drafts.walkScript: Start at 'pop!' on line 14. Line 15 says he was rolling 'in the warm grass of a great meadow'. So he came up in a meadow. Line 10 only compares his tunnel to a 'carriage-drive' that other animals own. The hedge and the river come later in the passage.

Find Mr Darcy at the end of line 39. Line 40 says he danced with Mrs Hurst 'once' and 'once with Miss Bingley'. One dance with each makes two dances. The words 'danced every dance' on line 37 describe Mr Bingley, not Mr Darcy.

Look at line 29, where John answers. He says they 'can't drive over that tree, nor yet get round it'. Line 30 gives the only way left: 'go back to the four crossways'. That way is 'a good six miles' before they reach the wooden bridge again. Nothing in these lines mentions waiting or walking home.

Look at line 13, where Jim is sent round to Mr Goggles. Pa sends kind regards and 'hopes his leg's better', across lines 13 and 14. That leg belongs to Mr Goggles, not to Pa. The one question comes on line 14: 'will he lend him his spirit-level'. So Jim goes to borrow the spirit-level.

Look at line 40, where Ilya says 'You've missed a cupboard'. Lines 40 and 41 place the other one 'In the annexe'. Line 41 then gives what Miss said about it. They can do 'that one on Monday' and 'get out of spellings'. Nothing here says it must be done before Friday.

Line 8 says there was 'no water in their room'. So they washed 'under the spout of the pump', across lines 9 and 10. Line 10 shares out the job: 'One pumped and the other washed'. So one works the pump while the other washes. It was 'splashy but interesting', so the splashing did not spoil it.

Line 21 says they 'could not find all the right things'. So they use other things in their place. Across lines 21 and 22, 'a glass ash-tray made an excellent salt-cellar'. Line 22 says 'a newish baking-tin' would do 'to put bread on'. The fire and kettle on line 20 are not things for the table.

Go to line 20 and find the word 'Below'. Line 20 says 'a boat lay in the mud with its ribs showing'. Line 21 adds 'a gull standing on it'. Then the words 'further along' on line 21 move on to the posts, somewhere else.
